init.title: Step 1 of 4 — Monitoring — Required entities
init.description: Map your inverter entities to Volter monitoring. These are required for energy optimization.

monitoring_extended.title: Step 2 of 4 — Monitoring — Optional entities
monitoring_extended.description: Additional entities for improved optimization accuracy.

control.title: Step 3 of 4 — Control — Inverter commands
control.description: Map inverter control entities to enable remote commands from the Volter app. All fields are optional.

data.entity_charge_limit: Battery power setpoint (W) — map EMS power limit
data.entity_eco_mode_soc: Lower SoC threshold — map the Depth of Discharge entity

data_description.entity_eco_mode_soc: On GoodWe point this at "Depth of Discharge (On-Grid)". The eco mode SoC entity is read-only, so writes there never reach the inverter. Volter converts the threshold to depth automatically.
data_description.entity_charge_limit: On GoodWe point this at "EMS power limit" (watts). It carries BOTH charge and discharge power.
data_description.entity_soc_upper: On GoodWe point this at "SoC upper limit". Without it the planner cannot say how far to charge.

strategy.title: Step 4 of 4 — Strategy — Guard parameters
strategy.description: These values drive the safety guards. SoC reserve is never crossed in Backup mode. Submitting this step saves the whole configuration.

data_description.control_enabled: When off, Volter computes the plan and logs every decision but writes NOTHING to the inverter. Leave it off until you have verified the mode mapping with the volter.diagnose action.
